title: RS485 module (MAX485), on the floor
summary: The JZK TTL-to-RS485 module has no mounting holes. It sits on a taped pedestal in an outline pocket with lead gaps at the bus end, the logic end and both long sides. In a closed box two lid pads press foam onto it, one inboard of each end's pin row.
firstUsed: Controller project (2026): room receiver and rack-ends

views.label: In the pocket
views.caption: Bus end (A+, B−, earth) on the left, logic end (VCC, TXD, RXD, GND) on the right, each with a 10 wide lead gap. Drag the slider to lift the board out.

views.label: Lid hold-down
views.caption: Two pads under the lid, 6 inboard of each end, press 3 mm foam onto the board, squashed by 1.

views.label: Fit piece
views.caption: Four pockets with a bridge where the logic-end lid pad would be, marked 1 to 4 dots: foam squeezed 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0. The ends are open so the board slides in under the foam.

specs.title: The module (JZK)
specs.note: Variants: XY-017 (42.8 × 15.22 × 0.8) and the classic MAX485 module with a screw terminal (44 × 14).

specs.title: The holder
rows: 10 at the ends, 6 in the sides
specs.badgeNote: the foam squeeze is set by the fit piece

checks: Slide the board in under the foam: can you, without forcing?
Does the foam hold it firmly, without bowing the board?
Give it a tug: does it stay put?
Does the foam spring back when you take the board out?
fit.print: Print base down, no supports, in the enclosure's material.
